entities.summary:
Catullus (b. 83 BCE, Verona) was a poet, playwright, and journalist of the Classical era, active in Verona. He wrote about his own life and the lives of his contemporaries, often using humor and satire. His poetry, known for its sensuality and emotional depth, influenced later Roman poets such as Virgil and Ovid.

Catullus' work often addressed themes of love, loss, and social class, making him a key figure in the literary and intellectual life of ancient Rome. His poetry also frequently referenced historical events and figures, such as Julius Caesar and Cicero.

Despite his significance in Roman literature, Catullus' life remains somewhat of a mystery. His exact date of death is unknown, but it is believed to have been around 53 BCE.

In the centuries following his death, Catullus' work was rediscovered and celebrated by Renaissance scholars, who saw him as a precursor to the great Renaissance poets.

Today, Catullus is recognized as one of the most important poets of the Classical era, and his work continues to be studied and admired by scholars and readers around the world.
